Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: l/www. dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 58 s. 2023 SEP 11 ATTY. EDUARDO M. PANGAN ATTY. DANIKA MARIE S. SANTOS Mendoza & Pangan Law Offices Unit II-I V. Madrigal Building 6793 Ayala Avenue, 1226 Makati City Dear Atty Pangan and Atty. Santos: This pertains to your letter dated 27 January 2023 concerning your client, Eramen Minerals, Inc. (EMI). What was requested is an advice on whether or not the Municipality of Infanta is entitled to a portion of the 70% business tax allocation on the basis of Eramen Mineral's transport of ore through the roads within its territorial jurisdiction and the loading of said ore at a port in Infanta, Pangasinan. The relevant facts submitted are as follows: • • EMI conducts its mining operations in Sta. Cruz, Zambales, entirely, and transports ore through the national highway connecting Sta. Cruz, Zambales to Infanta, Pangasinan, and loads its nickel ore onto vessels at a private port in Infanta, Pangasinan. The Municipality of Infanta is allegedly claiming entitlement to a portion of the 70% allocation of the business tax pursuant to Section 150 (b) of the Local Government Code, viz: (b) The following sales allocation shall apply to manufacturers, assemblers, contractors, producers% and exporters with factories, project offices, plants, and plantations in the pursuit of their business: (4) Thirty percent (30%) of all sales recorded in the principal office shall be taxable by the city or municipality where the principal office is located; and (5) Seventy percent (70%) of all sales recorded in the principal office shall be taxable by the city or municipality where the factory, project office, plant, or plantation is located. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

please be advised that with respect to the manner and the instances by which the 70% tax allocation provided under Section 150 (b)(5) of the Local Government Code may be shared, Section 150 (c) and (d) are controlling. To wit: (c) In case of a plantation located at a place other than the place where the factory is located, said seventy percent (70%) mentioned in subparagraph (b) of subsection (2) above shall be divided as follows: (1) Sixty percent (60%) to the city or municipality where the factory is located; and (2) Forty percent (40%) to the city or municipality where the plantation is located. (d) In case where a manufacturer, assembler, producer, exporter or contractor has two (2) or more factories, project offices, plants, or plantations located in different localities, the seventy percent (70%) mentioned in subparagraph (b) of subsection (2) above shall be prorated among the localities where the factories, project offices, plants, and plantations are located in proportion to their respective volume or production during the period for which the tax is due. Foregoing considered, the Municipality of Infanta is deemed entitled to a share of the 70% business tax only in case Eramen Minerals, Inc. maintains a factory, office, plant or plantation within its territorial jurisdiction other than the mine site located in Sta. Cruz, Zambales. We take cognizance of the submission that "a mine site from which ore is extracted is of the same class of locations as those enumerated in the foregoing provision, namely: "factory, project office, plant, or plantation". If what is meant by said statement is that Eramen Minerals, Inc. does not maintain any of those within the jurisdiction of Infanta, Pangasinan, and that the private port in Infanta Pangasinan where the ore is being loaded is not owned, operated and/or managed by Eramen Minerals Inc., then the concerned municipality is not entitled to a share of the 70% business tax. Further, please be informed that any imposition for the transport of goods through the boundaries of a local government unit constitute an imposition of pass through fees which is suspended by virtue of DILG MC No. 2018-133, THE OMNIBUS GUIDELINES ON THE SUSPENSION OF LGU IMPOSITION AND COLLECTION OF ILLEGAL FEES AND TAXES RELATIVE TO THE TRANSPORT OF GOODS AND PRODUCTS. This opinion is based solely on the facts and representations narrated in the letter and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and courts. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Thank you.

Very truly yours, By th Authority of the Secretary: AT UANV OR R. LLAMAS d secretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs LLD/CLP/kbm copy furnished: ATTY. ANTHONY C. NUYDA, CESO Ill Regional Director, DILG Region-III Diosdado Macapagal Government Center Maimpis, San Fernando City, Pampanga
